chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Ibn Abi Yafur who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and made her dower her father, on condition that she return to him one thousand dirhams. Then he divorced her before consummating the marriage. What is appropriate for her to return to him? And indeed, she is entitled to half the dower. Her father is an old man, his value is five hundred dirhams, and he says, 'If it were not for you, I would not have sold him for three thousand dirhams.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No consideration is given to his words, and she does not return to him anything.'

key_terms.قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: before he consummates the marriage with her
key_terms.لَا يُنْظَرُ فِي قَوْلِهِ: no consideration is given to his words

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning dower when a woman is divorced before consummation and the dower was her father?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial settlement for a woman divorced before consummation, specifically addressing a scenario where the dower was a specific person (her father) rather than a fixed sum. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the father’s subjective claim of value (e.g., 3,000 dirhams) is not binding on the husband, so the woman returns only the standard half-dower without additional compensation based on the father's valuation. This ruling underscores the principle that subjective assessments of a person's 'price' do not alter the fixed legal entitlements of the wife in cases of pre-consummation divorce.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who married a woman and made her dower to be her father upon that a thousand Dirhams would be returned to him. Then he divorces her before he sleeps with her. What is befitting for her that she should return to him? And rather, for her is half the dower, and her father is an old man. His value is five hundred Dirhams, and he is saying, ‘Were it not for you, I would not sell him with three thousand Dirhams’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There would be no consideration for his words, and nothing would be returned to him’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman and has set her father as her mahr (dower) and that she must return one thousand dirham to him. He then divorces her before going to bed with her. What must she return to him when she deserves only one- half of the mahr (dower )? Her father is an old man who is worth only five hundred dirham and he says, ’Were it not because of you I would not sell him for three thousand dirham. He (the Imam) said, ‘His words are not considered and nothing is returned to him.’”
